alloy.preparation: Cylindrical electrode 0.25 in. diameter × 0.75 in. long, machined from solution-annealed stock. Standard polarization preparation: abrade through 2.0 emery paper, wash in detergent, rinse with distilled water, dry; Stern–Mackrides-type holder in glass cell.

test_solution.preparation: Reagent-grade 1 M NaCl in distilled water; final pH 6.3 at 25 °C. Hydrogen-saturated condition. H2 flow 1.5 l/min, reported residual dissolved oxygen 0.076 ppm.

test_method.procedure_description: Glass cell, bright-Pt auxiliary electrodes, SCE reference through Luggin–Haber probe; no liquid-junction-potential correction. 600 ml electrolyte; specimen exposed for 60 min before continuous scan in the noble direction at 0.600 V/hr. Continuous scan is distinct from cited authors’ stepped procedure. Table II gas-dependent critical-breakdown results are the authors’ measurements, summarized from their prior report; only present-PDF context is used.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Critical breakdown of passivity Ec on anodic scan, associated with pit initiation; prolonged exposure at potentials more noble than Ec produces severe pitting, without observed crevice corrosion.

experiments.result_note: Reproducibility stated as ±10 mV for repeated polarization curves; not a separately tabulated statistical uncertainty. The text describes these as the authors’ experiments, previously reported in reference (20) and summarized in Table II. Table I w/o analyses retained; ND means not determined and remains null. No Fe residual/commercial recipe is calculated. Thermostatic test temperature 25 ±1 °C is reported; solution-annealing temperature/time is not. Ec is critical breakdown, not Ecorr, a repassivation potential, or the FeCl3-exposure maximum/minimum corrosion potentials. ±10 mV repeatability is not a new statistical error bar on every outcome.

test_solution.preparation: Reagent-grade 1 M NaCl in distilled water; final pH 6.3 at 25 °C. Oxygen-saturated condition. O2 flow 1.5 l/min.

test_method.procedure_description: Glass cell, bright-Pt auxiliary electrodes, SCE reference through Luggin–Haber probe; no liquid-junction-potential correction. Same Type 430 specimen first exposed in oxygen-saturated 1 M NaCl for 100 h at steady corrosion potential about −0.140 V SCE without pitting, then connected to potentiostat and held at −0.140 V for a further 100 h without pitting. This registered lower test bound refers to the second, potentiostatic oxygenated 100 h period.
test_method.pitting_criterion: No pitting during oxygenated 100 h potentiostatic exposure; protocol-specific test lower bound.

experiments.result_note: No pitting at −0.140 V during the potentiostatic oxygenated hold: protocol-specific lower test bound. Same sample subsequently pits after hydrogen substitution; this is a separate altered-environment outcome. Table I w/o analyses retained; ND means not determined and remains null. No Fe residual/commercial recipe is calculated. Thermostatic test temperature 25 ±1 °C is reported; solution-annealing temperature/time is not. Ec is critical breakdown, not Ecorr, a repassivation potential, or the FeCl3-exposure maximum/minimum corrosion potentials. ±10 mV repeatability is not a new statistical error bar on every outcome.

alloy.preparation: Cylindrical electrode 0.25 in. diameter × 0.75 in. long, machined from solution-annealed stock. Standard polarization preparation: abrade through 2.0 emery paper, wash in detergent, rinse with distilled water, dry; Stern–Mackrides-type holder in glass cell.

test_solution.preparation: Reagent-grade 1 M NaCl in distilled water; final pH 6.3 at 25 °C. Hydrogen following oxygen exposure-saturated condition. Oxygen flow replaced by H2 at 1.50 l/min without interrupting imposed potential.

test_method.procedure_description: Glass cell, bright-Pt auxiliary electrodes, SCE reference through Luggin–Haber probe; no liquid-junction-potential correction. Same Type 430 specimen first exposed in oxygen-saturated 1 M NaCl for 100 h at steady corrosion potential about −0.140 V SCE without pitting, then connected to potentiostat and held at −0.140 V for a further 100 h without pitting. With potential still imposed, oxygen was replaced by hydrogen at 1.50 l/min; after 16 h pronounced pitting with rapid anodic-current increase occurred. The full preceding oxygenated history is retained, rather than treating this as a fresh hydrogen-saturated scan.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Pronounced pitting accompanied by rapid anodic-current increase after 16 h of hydrogen substitution at unchanged −0.140 V SCE; supplies an upper bound, not an exact scan breakdown.

experiments.result_note: Observed pitting at this hold potential after 16 h gives only Epit ≤−0.140 V for this history, not an exact breakdown potential; distinct from gas-saturated scan results. Table I w/o analyses retained; ND means not determined and remains null. No Fe residual/commercial recipe is calculated. Thermostatic test temperature 25 ±1 °C is reported; solution-annealing temperature/time is not. Ec is critical breakdown, not Ecorr, a repassivation potential, or the FeCl3-exposure maximum/minimum corrosion potentials. ±10 mV repeatability is not a new statistical error bar on every outcome.
